description: A small, MIT-licensed PDF writer for reports: paragraphs and tables with pagination, vector drawing, embedded font subsets, right-to-left and mixed-direction text, and Arabic, Indic and Thai shaping through HarfBuzz. Tables stream their rows, headers and footers know the page count, and a drawing canvas and a text measurer serve charts. Fonts are supplied by the caller, never looked up in the operating system, and the text of the file reads back in logical order.
releaseNotes:
0.1.7: less memory and faster saves, with the same output byte for byte. A 1,000-row table allocates 8.1 MB per save instead of 18.3 MB, a fresh process that saves it peaks about 4.5 MB lower (43.7 MB with ReadyToRun), and a warm save takes about 15 to 25 percent less time. SHA-256 is computed in managed code, so an ordinary document no longer loads System.Security.Cryptography. New: FontCollection.AddFile(path) and Add(Stream) read a font straight into the collection without a copy held by the caller.

0.1.6: tagged (accessible) PDF, on by default. Every document is written with a structure tree in reading order (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables with column headers, figures with their AltText as alternative text; headers, footers, fills, borders and pictures without AltText as artifacts) and the languages of its runs, and claims PDF/UA-1 when it has a title and a language and nothing is reported; DocumentDiagnostics.IsPdfUA and AccessibilityIssues say whether, and why not. veraPDF validates PDF/UA-1 in CI. Tagged = false writes the bytes of 0.1.5. Tagged files are larger (about 1.15 to 2.5 times; a 1,000-row table 186 KB against 76 KB), so a MaxBytes limit sized for 0.1.5 may need raising; allocation is about the same and a warm 1,000-row table takes about 15 ms more.

0.1.5: a faster first save in a fresh process and a smaller working set, with the same output, byte for byte. Less code is compiled on the first save (a 1,000-row table: 492 ms to 417 ms from process start to exit, and 310 ms to 240 ms when the application is published with ReadyToRun), and HarfBuzz reads the font collection's copy of a font instead of keeping a native copy of its own (the table's peak working set 53 MB to 50 MB). The benchmarks gain the plan's 20-page report, a 100-page stress document, Arabic and Hindi tables and a 10,000-row table, and the tests hold their allocation to budgets.

0.1.4: faster and lighter saves with the same output, byte for byte (a 1,000-row table, warm: about 136 ms to 55 ms and 59 MB to 18.5 MB allocated per save). Printable ASCII is shaped word by word with a per-font word cache in fonts whose layout rules never involve the space, glyph positions are written without the custom number format, layout arrays are pooled, and ASCII text skips the general Unicode passes it does not need. The guide has a new section on startup time (ReadyToRun: a first save in a fresh process about a third faster).

0.1.3: a zero width joiner or non-joiner at the end of a line is no longer missing from the extracted text; text shaping and layout are faster and allocate less (a 1,000-row table: about 82 MB to 59 MB per save); the output is unchanged.

0.1.2: PdfImage.FromBytes reads WebP pictures (lossy, lossless and with alpha; an animated WebP is refused), decoded in managed code with no new dependency. Files are much smaller (a 1,000-row table: 514 KB to 76 KB) with the same glyph positions, and writing a page allocates about half as much; the text reads back as before in PdfPig and pdf.js.

0.1.1: a line break or another control character in a string no longer makes a save throw. Every line break (\n, \r\n, \r, U+0085, U+000B, U+000C, U+001C to U+001E, U+2028, U+2029) is a hard line break inside the same block, everywhere text is laid out (canvas text included); other control characters are removed; a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD; metadata, font family and language strings are trimmed and cleaned. Text without these characters is written as before.

0.1.0, the first release: a PDF writer for reports. Blocks (Heading, Paragraph, Table, ItemList, Columns, Callout, Drawing, Image) flow and paginate; tables stream their rows and repeat the header; a drawing canvas and a text measurer serve charts; headers and footers know the page count; fonts are supplied by the caller and embedded as subsets; right-to-left and mixed-direction text, and Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil and Thai shaping through HarfBuzz, are written in logical order so the text can be searched and copied; output is deterministic; SaveAsync can be cancelled; PdfImageOptions limits picture size (40 megapixels by default).

Known limitations (0.1.x): the language review of the test text was made by an AI agent, not by native speakers (Tamil, Bengali, Thai and Marathi least certain); the viewer check was PDFium renders, and Acrobat Reader and macOS Preview were not checked; the size and allocation targets and the warm times of the Latin documents are met (the tagged 1,000-row table is 186 KB against the 150 KB aimed at untagged), but a first save with the default JIT is over the cold target and the Arabic and Hindi tables are about 5 and 6 times the Latin table's time against the 2 times aimed at (docs/baselines.md); tagged PDF is validated by veraPDF only, not by hand with a screen reader; CJK fonts with TrueType outlines are accepted but not tested, and fonts with CFF outlines (Noto Sans CJK, Source Han) are not supported yet.

Full notes: https://github.com/sinanoran/pdfwright/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
